answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Not yet. 40 miles next week is more than three times last week's 12, so the plan is 18 easy miles and no speedwork.

Feeling ready is a good sign, but heart and lungs bounce back before legs do. The first hard session after a marathon is where setbacks tend to start, and one more steady week costs you very little.

You also don't need 40 miles to run a good 10K, because the base from your marathon build carries over. Here is the rough path if you race it, and I'll adjust it as the weeks go:

| Week | Easy miles | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 26 – Nov 1 | 18 | All easy, a few strides, one short strength session |
| Nov 2 – 8 | about 24 | All easy, strides twice, a longer Sunday run |
| Nov 9 – 15 | about 30 | First short session at 10K effort |
| Nov 16 – 22 | about 32 | One sharpening session, everything else easy |

new.analysis:
Last week went exactly to plan. You ran all three runs at the planned 3, 4 and 5 miles, with pain at 0/10 and not a minute above easy heart rate zones. Sunday's 5 miles at 139 bpm and 9:51 per mile matches your easy running from before the race, so the legs are recovering on schedule.

This week raises volume by about half instead of tripling it. Your recovery is working, and a calm few weeks now protects the next block of training. Your 40-mile base is real and won't disappear, so there is no fitness to chase.

The week is boring on purpose. Four runs at easy heart rate, Monday and Friday kept as rest days, and a light strength session in the slot where your Wednesday session used to sit. Strength is the cheapest way to build the leg durability that faded for you after mile 20 on race day.

The race itself was a solid step forward. About 3:50 is 12 minutes faster than your first marathon, and you were on pace through 20 miles. You missed the under 3:45 target by about 5 minutes, and the late fade is something a future marathon build can fix.

What I need from you now is your next goal. Tell me if you're racing the Thanksgiving 10K, along with the date and the time you want. A 10K on that timeline is realistic, but I'd settle the target time after two more clean weeks.

If you're not racing it, we keep building easy volume for a few weeks and then pick a goal together. A spring marathon with more marathon-pace work in the long runs would be one option.
